## Background
Owner source conversation: codex:01a1175d-c148-70c1-92d8-588826ff4234, turns 1–10. Arbitrary text is already accepted by the shared synthesize() registry, but voice:say is short-reply oriented and ordinary desktop playback uses a 200-character preview route; the full-reply route slices at 4000. Truncation defect: EI-25342308956200572 (held by this session; source-path finding, not yet a live audio repro).

## Design
Extend existing surfaces rather than build another speech/agent stack:
- One authorized/bounded content representation for extracted text and source references, shared by narration and summary consumers. Agents may supply already-read content; remote/file/document retrieval reuses existing permission-bearing readers and must not introduce unrestricted server-side fetching. Selected text is first class. HTML uses Mozilla Readability and text-bearing PDFs use PDF.js if existing readers do not cover them; scanned sources expose an OCR/access limitation, not invented content.
- Keep synthesize(), voice preferences, release availability, existing local Kokoro port and playback lease/mute seams. Intl.Segmenter supplies sentence boundaries, with provider-size splitting of unusually long sentences. Speech is nonoverlapping and lossless. No second Kokoro/Transformers stack.
- Extend voice:say with explicit narration/session behavior while preserving backwards-compatible short replies. UI uses existing output-only playback and maintained controls. Add controls to existing voice surfaces rather than invent a new app/screen scaffold.
- Normal speech uses a production synthesis path, never settings-preview truncation. Incremental synthesis uses bounded backpressure, cancellation and explicit lifecycle receipts. The chosen provider is stable for a reading; current settings apply when the next reading starts. Never silently change local speech into cloud speech.
- Summaries use the existing model/account gateway and budget/task primitives. Direct native-agent summaries remain direct when complete input already fits the active context. Large/repeatable jobs use structure/token-aware segmentation and hierarchical synthesis, with source references and explicit coverage/limitations. A framework is not a better brain: @langchain/textsplitters is an optional narrow helper; LlamaIndex tree-summarize is a reference pattern, not a mandatory new Python service.
- Cache only by authorized subject, source hash/version, summary options and effective model/protocol. Bound/cancel jobs using existing task manager rather than a second queue. Treat extracted material as quoted untrusted data, never execution instructions.
- Original read and summary-and-read are distinct modes. Preserve the original content and make edits/omissions explicit.
